classification.difficultyReason: Follow the prescribed direct surface-area/volume calculations and squared/cubed scale-factor alternatives across four familiar solids, including a Pythagorean slant height.

inlines.text: i  Find what factor the total surface area of the smaller solid must be multiplied by in order to obtain the surface area of the larger solid. In parts a and c, do this by finding the surface areas; in parts b and d, use the enlargement factor method.

ii  Find what factor the volume of the smaller solid must be multiplied by in order to obtain the volume of the larger solid. In parts b and d, do this by finding the volumes; in parts a and c, use the enlargement factor method.

answer.worked:
The radii are $2\text{ cm}$ and $3\text{ cm}$.

$$\begin{align*}V_{\text{small}}&=\pi\times2^2\times4\\V_{\text{small}}&=16\pi\text{ cm}^3\\V_{\text{large}}&=\pi\times3^2\times6\\V_{\text{large}}&=54\pi\text{ cm}^3\\\text{Volume factor}&=\frac{54\pi}{16\pi}\\\text{Volume factor}&=\frac{27}{8}\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$\frac{36}{25}$

Find each total surface area using $S=\pi r^2+\pi r\ell$, then divide larger by smaller.
answer.worked:
The radii are $4\text{ cm}$ and $4.8\text{ cm}$. Use Pythagoras’ theorem to find the slant heights.

$$\begin{align*}\ell_{\text{small}}&=\sqrt{10^2+4^2}\\\ell_{\text{small}}&=2\sqrt{29}\text{ cm}\\\ell_{\text{large}}&=\sqrt{12^2+4.8^2}\\\ell_{\text{large}}&=\frac{12\sqrt{29}}5\text{ cm}\\S_{\text{small}}&=\pi\times4^2+\pi\times4\times2\sqrt{29}\\S_{\text{small}}&=(16+8\sqrt{29})\pi\text{ cm}^2\\S_{\text{large}}&=\pi\left(\frac{24}{5}\right)^2+\pi\times\frac{24}{5}\times\frac{12\sqrt{29}}5\\S_{\text{large}}&=\frac{(576+288\sqrt{29})\pi}{25}\text{ cm}^2\\\text{Surface area factor}&=\frac{(576+288\sqrt{29})\pi}{25(16+8\sqrt{29})\pi}\\\text{Surface area factor}&=\frac{36}{25}\end{align*}$$
